front: Which homologous series has the functional group -COOH?
back: Carboxylic acids.

front: What is the functional group of an alcohol?
back: An -OH group bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

front: Which homologous series contains a carbon-nitrogen triple bond?
back: Nitriles. The carbon atom of the nitrile group is bonded to the rest of the molecule.

front: Which class of compounds includes molecules with an -NH2 group bonded to an alkyl group?
back: Primary amines.

front: What is the name of the -CH3 substituent?
back: Methyl.

front: What is the structural formula of propane?
back: CH3CH2CH3

front: What is the molecular formula of hex-1-ene?
back: C6H12

front: What suffix is used when naming a carboxylic acid?
back: The suffix is -oic acid, as in ethanoic acid.

front: What ending is used for the acid-derived part of an ester name?
back: The ending is -oate, as in ethyl ethanoate.

front: What suffix and prefix are used to name an -OH group?
back:
The suffix is -ol, as in ethanol.
The prefix is hydroxy- when a higher-priority functional group determines the suffix.

front: How can the structure of an ester be written using R groups?
back:
R-C(=O)-O-R'
R and R' represent organic groups that may be different. In a methanoate ester, the group attached to the carbonyl carbon is H instead of R.

front: What class of compounds has the structure R-O-R'?
back: Ethers.

front: What is the structural difference between an aldehyde and a ketone?
back:
An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon bonded to at least one H atom: -CHO.
A ketone has a carbonyl carbon bonded to two carbon atoms.

front: What is the functional group of an alkene?
back: A carbon-carbon double bond, C=C.

front: What type of carbon-carbon bonds are present in an alkane?
back: Single covalent bonds only.

front: What group is present in both aldehydes and ketones?
back: The carbonyl group, C=O.

front: What suffix is used when naming a ketone?
back: The suffix is -one, as in propanone.

front: What suffix is used when naming an aldehyde?
back: The suffix is -al, as in ethanal.

front: What is a functional group?
back: An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic chemical reactions of an organic compound.

front: What is a homologous series?
back:
A family of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula.
Successive members differ by CH2 and have similar chemical properties.

front: What does a displayed formula show?
back: Every atom and every bond in a molecule.

front: How do you choose the numbering direction when naming a simple branched alkane?
back:
Number the parent chain to give the branches the lowest possible set of numbers.
Compare the sets at the first point where they differ.

front: How do you choose the parent chain of a simple branched alkane?
back:
Choose the longest continuous carbon chain.
The number of carbon atoms in that chain determines the stem of the name.

front: What does R represent in an organic formula?
back:
An unspecified organic group, usually an alkyl group.
It is shorthand for part of the molecule.

front: What is an alkyl group?
back:
A group formed by removing one H atom from an alkane.
For example, methane gives the methyl group, -CH3.

front: What is a haloalkane?
back: A compound formed when one or more H atoms in an alkane are replaced by halogen atoms.

front: Which homologous series has the functional group -C(=O)Cl?
back: Acyl chlorides.

front: What is an alkane?
back:
A saturated, acyclic hydrocarbon.
It contains only carbon and hydrogen, with single bonds only.

front: What ending is used when naming an acyl chloride?
back: The ending is -oyl chloride, as in ethanoyl chloride.

front: What is a general formula?
back:
An algebraic formula describing members of a homologous series.
For example, the general formula of alkanes is CnH(2n+2).

front: What is an empirical formula?
back: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.

front: What is a molecular formula?
back: The actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule.

front: What does a structural formula show?
back:
The arrangement of atoms or groups in a molecule, without showing every bond.
For example, CH3CH2OH is the structural formula of ethanol.
